scenes.heading: Using congruence in quadrilaterals
scenes.say: You know that opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal. But why? Draw one diagonal, find two congruent triangles, and the reason appears. Let's prove the properties of quadrilaterals and use them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cut a paper parallelogram on a diagonal and spin one half
scenes.science: The two triangles are congruent, so matching sides are equal
scenes.breaks: Cutting paper shows it for one shape. A congruence proof works for every parallelogram.
scenes.say: Cut out a paper parallelogram and slice along a diagonal. Spin one triangle a half turn and it sits exactly on the other. They're congruent, so the sides they came from must be equal. Paper only shows it for one shape, but a proof works for every parallelogram.

scenes.heading: The method
steps: Name: SSS, SAS, AAS or RHS
scenes.say: Here's the method. Split the shape with a diagonal. Match three pairs of equal parts, looking for alternate angles, shared sides and vertically opposite angles. Name the test. Then conclude the property.

scenes.heading: Find the Z inside a parallelogram
notes: AC is common to both triangles
scenes.say: First the parallelogram, then the diagonal A C, then the angle marks. The parallel sides make two Z shapes, so the angles with one arc are equal, and so are the angles with two arcs. Add the shared side A C and the triangles are congruent.

scenes.heading: Parallelogram proof
scenes.question: Prove opposite sides of parallelogram PQRS are equal.
lines: So PQ = RS and QR = SP
scenes.say: Draw diagonal P R. Because the sides are parallel, we get two pairs of alternate angles. P R is shared by both triangles. So the triangles are congruent by A S A, and the matching sides P Q and R S are equal, as are Q R and S P.
scenes.caption: Draw diagonal PR. Parallel sides give two pairs of alternate angles. PR is common. So the triangles are congruent (ASA), and PQ = RS, QR = SP.

scenes.heading: What congruence proves
points: Kite: one pair of opposite angles equal
scenes.say: Using the same idea: a parallelogram's diagonals bisect each other. A rectangle's diagonals are equal. A rhombus's diagonals cross at right angles. And a kite has one pair of equal opposite angles.

scenes.heading: Rhombus diagonals cross at 90°
scenes.say: Here's a rhombus with diagonals of twenty-four and ten centimetres. First the shape, then the diagonals, crossing at a right angle in the middle. Each diagonal is cut in half, so every little triangle has legs of twelve and five centimetres.

scenes.heading: Rhombus perimeter
scenes.question: A rhombus has diagonals of 10 cm and 24 cm. Find its perimeter.
scenes.say: A rhombus has diagonals of ten and twenty-four centimetres. They bisect each other at right angles, so use the halves: five and twelve. Pythagoras gives a side of thirteen centimetres. All four sides are equal, so the perimeter is fifty-two centimetres.
scenes.caption: Diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. Halves: 5 and 12. Pythagoras: side = √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm. Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52 cm.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Split the shape, match three parts, name the test and conclude. Parallel sides give alternate angles. A shared side is free evidence. And in a rhombus, halve the diagonals before using Pythagoras. Now try the practice questions!
